page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-32 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon processors running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance provisions 32 vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Memory capacity totals 208 GB, delivering a dense ratio of 6.5 GB per vCPU. The CPU subsystem includes 45 MB of shared L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1 data cache per core, alongside standard instruction flags such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA. No discrete GPU acceleration is included, and the instance is provisioned without local storage, necessitating external persistent disks for file storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear split between single-threaded execution and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance metrics are modest, with Geekbench single-core at 936.0 and stress-ng single-core measuring 1114.88, placing it in the lower percentiles. Conversely, parallel performance shows solid scaling: multi-core Geekbench reaches 8358.0 and stress-ng multi-core hits 23345.66. Memory bandwidth evaluates at 95.75 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 44.06 GB/sec for large block writes, complemented by a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 54.66 GB/sec and a PassMark CPU score of 22466.6.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the n1-highmem-32 trades absolute per-thread instruction velocity for substantial memory density and multi-core scalability. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage and absence of AVX-512 extensions restrict its value for modern heavy matrix computation or high-throughput local disk IOPS scenarios. However, the 208 GB RAM footprint and multi-threaded throughput make it a practical platform for in-memory caching solutions like Redis (achieving 21.74 million SET operations per second), relational database hosts, and medium-scale web serving environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-32 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon x86_64 architecture clocked at 2.3 GHz) and 208 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network storage. Benchmark profiles reveal modest single-thread capacity—scoring 936.0 on Geekbench single-core and 1114.88 on single-core stress-ng—balanced by solid multi-core performance, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 22466.6 and Geekbench multi-core score of 8358.0. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 95.75 GB/sec alongside write speeds of 44.06 GB/sec. This configuration offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy operations, excelling in multi-threaded tasks, in-memory databases like Redis, and memory-intensive enterprise services.
